member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ICalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceAutoCalibration(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientProjectorInfoDto)
member.summary: Triggers an Automatic Alignment (or FlashAlign) attempt with the specified projector.
member.remarks: Launches an Automatic Alignment of this projector; if the projector is vision capable, attempts a FlashAlign; same action as \"Locate Targets Automatically\" in Iris Client > Projector Dashboard > Targets Tab > Alignment Controls, or via Projected Menus; see \"Performing an Automatic Alignment\" in Iris Operator Guide. The projector will use any previously remembered target scan locations to predict where the targets are; if that fails (either there are no saved target scan locations or the tool targets are outside of the predicted search locations), the system will abandon the Automatic / FlashAlignment. <example> ClientProjectorInfoDto { ClientId (string, required), ProjectorSerial (string, required) } </example>
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call
member.param: the client and projector information data

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ICalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceGetCalibrationDetail(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientProjectorInfoDto)
member.summary: Returns detailed alignment information for the specified projector.
member.remarks: Provides additional information that may be used to diagnose and troubleshoot a projector's poor alignment error (GetCalibrationError): <example> CalibrationDetailDto { SerialNumber (string, optional), MaximumError (number, optional), RMSError (number, optional), CalibrationTolerance (number, optional), FailReason (string, optional), TotalAlignmentTargets (integer, optional), LocatedReferenceTargetCount (integer, optional) } </example> * **MaximumError** - worst target alignment error (in Feet) - this is also the value returned in `/GetCalibrationError` * **RMSError** - RMS error (Feet)of all targets currently scannable by the laser projector * **CalibrationTolerance** - the ALIGNMENT tolerance (in Feet) in use by this projector for target scans; corresponds to Maximum Alignment Error specified in Virtek Server Manager under Server (global) or Iris Client: Alignment Options or in Iris Client > Work Order Options. * **FailReason** - if the projector has failed alignment, this error string may indicate why. * **TotalAlignmentTargets** - total number of Work Order targets (of type Alignment, Drift, Required) available for use in this Work Order (but not necessarily what can be seen by this projector) * **LocatedReferenceTargetCount** - number of targets from the Total above which this projector has scanned successfully (to within tolerances.)
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.summary: Returns detailed alignment information for the specified projector.
member.remarks: Provides additional information that may be used to diagnose and troubleshoot a projector's poor alignment error (GetCalibrationError): <example> CalibrationDetailDto { SerialNumber (string, optional), MaximumError (number, optional), RMSError (number, optional), CalibrationTolerance (number, optional), FailReason (string, optional), TotalAlignmentTargets (integer, optional), LocatedReferenceTargetCount (integer, optional) } </example> * **MaximumError** - worst target alignment error (in Feet) - this is also the value returned in `/GetCalibrationError` * **RMSError** - RMS error (Feet)of all targets currently scannable by the laser projector * **CalibrationTolerance** - the ALIGNMENT tolerance (in Feet) in use by this projector for target scans; corresponds to Maximum Alignment Error specified in Virtek Server Manager under Server (global) or Iris Client: Alignment Options or in Iris Client > Work Order Options. * **FailReason** - if the projector has failed alignment, this error string may indicate why. * **TotalAlignmentTargets** - total number of Work Order targets (of type Alignment, Drift, Required) available for use in this Work Order (but not necessarily what can be seen by this projector) * **LocatedReferenceTargetCount** - number of targets from the Total above which this projector has scanned successfully (to within tolerances.)
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ICalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceGetCalibrationError(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientProjectorInfoDto)
member.summary: Retrieves the current alignment error of the specified projector to its observable alignment targets.
member.remarks: Shows the maximum/worst case alignment error (in Feet) of the specified projector to its observable alignment targets, based on laser scans of those targets; this is the same number that is shown at the top of Iris Client > Projector Dashboard > Targets Tab, and matches the worst individual target alignment error shown in that tab. While this is technically an \"alignment\" error, use of the term \"calibration\" is historical.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ICalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceGetModelPosition(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientProjectorInfoDto)
member.summary: Returns model (tool) location and orientation in projector coordinates.
member.remarks: Returns x,y,z projector space coordinates of the model (tool) origin (in FEET), and rotation (in radians) about each of the x,y and z axes for orientation. If the projector is not been aligned in this Work Order then any position/orientation returned by this method is to be disregarded.

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ICalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceGetProjectorAlignmentState(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientProjectorInfoDto)
member.summary: Returns the Alignment Status of the specified projector.
member.remarks: Returns the projector's AlignmentState (also available from `/GetProjectorDescriptors`) See `ProjectorDescriptorDto` > `AlignmentState` in the Integrators Guide. ProjectorAlignmentState values indicating the specified projector's current state are as follows: - (-1) Unknown - The projector was not found in an open work order for the client id or an alignment attempt has not taken place - ( 0) Error - Alignment attempt has not succeeded; either targets could not be found or not scanned to within required tolerances (RED) - ( 1) Aligning - LED flashes are in progress (if using vision capable projectors aka FlashAlign) and/or lasers are scanning Work Order Tool targets. a projector in the midst of Manual Alignment will show this as well. - ( 2) Aligned - Lasers have aligned to the Work Order using the tool targets to within tolerance specifications (GREEN) - ( 3) Warning - Lasers have scanned tool targets, but the vision system is impaired (possibly CalibrationState=FailedCalibration) (YELLOW) - ( 4) Excluded - The projector is excluded from participating in the Work Order (BLACK)
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call
member.param: Contains the Client Id and the serial number of the projector.

member.summary: Returns the Alignment Status of the specified projector.
member.remarks: Returns the projector's AlignmentState (also available from `/GetProjectorDescriptors`) See `ProjectorDescriptorDto` > `AlignmentState` in the Integrators Guide. ProjectorAlignmentState values indicating the specified projector's current state are as follows: - (-1) Unknown - The projector was not found in an open work order for the client id or an alignment attempt has not taken place - ( 0) Error - Alignment attempt has not succeeded; either targets could not be found or not scanned to within required tolerances (RED) - ( 1) Aligning - LED flashes are in progress (if using vision capable projectors aka FlashAlign) and/or lasers are scanning Work Order Tool targets. a projector in the midst of Manual Alignment will show this as well. - ( 2) Aligned - Lasers have aligned to the Work Order using the tool targets to within tolerance specifications (GREEN) - ( 3) Warning - Lasers have scanned tool targets, but the vision system is impaired (possibly CalibrationState=FailedCalibration) (YELLOW) - ( 4) Excluded - The projector is excluded from participating in the Work Order (BLACK)
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call
member.param: Contains the Client Id and the serial number of the projector.

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ICalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceTargetProjection(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.TargetProjectionDto)
member.summary: Sets on/off \"Project All Targets\" or \"Show Labels\" for the specified projector.
member.remarks: Sets the projection of remembered target locations by a specific projector on (ProjectTargets=true) or off (false); same as clicking the \"Project All Targets\" button in the projector's Projector Dashboard > Targets Tab. If ShowLabels is true, will also display the target name label as if the \"Show Labels\" checkbox was enabled under the Project All Targets button. ShowLabels is ignored if `ProjectTargets=false`. <example> TargetProjectionDto { ClientInfo (ClientInfoDto, required), ProjectorSerial (string, required), ProjectTargets (boolean, required), ShowLabels (boolean, required) } ClientInfoDto { ClientId (string, required), OriginatingClientGuid (string, optional), Type (string, optional) } </example>
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.remarks: Sets the projection of remembered target locations by a specific projector on (ProjectTargets=true) or off (false); same as clicking the \"Project All Targets\" button in the projector's Projector Dashboard > Targets Tab. member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.CalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceAutoCalibration(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientProjectorInfoDto)
member.summary: Triggers an Automatic Alignment (or FlashAlign) attempt with the specified projector. Launches an Automatic Alignment of this projector; if the projector is vision capable, attempts a FlashAlign; same action as \"Locate Targets Automatically\" in Iris Client > Projector Dashboard > Targets Tab > Alignment Controls, or via Projected Menus; see \"Performing an Automatic Alignment\" in Iris Operator Guide. The projector will use any previously remembered target scan locations to predict where the targets are; if that fails (either there are no saved target scan locations or the tool targets are outside of the predicted search locations), the system will abandon the Automatic / FlashAlignment. <example> ClientProjectorInfoDto { ClientId (string, required), ProjectorSerial (string, required) } </example>
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call
member.param: the client and projector information data

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.CalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceGetCalibrationDetail(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientProjectorInfoDto)
member.summary: Returns detailed alignment information for the specified projector. Provides additional information that may be used to diagnose and troubleshoot a projector's poor alignment error (GetCalibrationError): <example> CalibrationDetailDto { SerialNumber (string, optional), MaximumError (number, optional), RMSError (number, optional), CalibrationTolerance (number, optional), FailReason (string, optional), TotalAlignmentTargets (integer, optional), LocatedReferenceTargetCount (integer, optional) } </example> * **MaximumError** - worst target alignment error (in Feet) - this is also the value returned in `/GetCalibrationError` * **RMSError** - RMS error (Feet)of all targets currently scannable by the laser projector * **CalibrationTolerance** - the ALIGNMENT tolerance (in Feet) in use by this projector for target scans; corresponds to Maximum Alignment Error specified in Virtek Server Manager under Server (global) or Iris Client: Alignment Options or in Iris Client > Work Order Options. * **FailReason** - if the projector has failed alignment, this error string may indicate why. * **TotalAlignmentTargets** - total number of Work Order targets (of type Alignment, Drift, Required) available for use in this Work Order (but not necessarily what can be seen by this projector) * **LocatedReferenceTargetCount** - number of targets from the Total above which this projector has scanned successfully (to within tolerances.)
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.CalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceGetCalibrationError(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientProjectorInfoDto)
member.summary: Retrieves the current alignment error of the specified projector to its observable alignment targets. Shows the maximum/worst case alignment error (in Feet) of the specified projector to its observable alignment targets, based on laser scans of those targets; this is the same number that is shown at the top of Iris Client > Projector Dashboard > Targets Tab, and matches the worst individual target alignment error shown in that tab. While this is technically an \"alignment\" error, use of the term \"calibration\" is historical.

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.CalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceGetProjectorAlignmentState(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientProjectorInfoDto)
member.summary: Returns the Alignment Status of the specified projector. Returns the projector's AlignmentState (also available from `/GetProjectorDescriptors`) See `ProjectorDescriptorDto` > `AlignmentState` in the Integrators Guide. ProjectorAlignmentState values indicating the specified projector's current state are as follows: - (-1) Unknown - The projector was not found in an open work order for the client id or an alignment attempt has not taken place - ( 0) Error - Alignment attempt has not succeeded; either targets could not be found or not scanned to within required tolerances (RED) - ( 1) Aligning - LED flashes are in progress (if using vision capable projectors aka FlashAlign) and/or lasers are scanning Work Order Tool targets. a projector in the midst of Manual Alignment will show this as well. - ( 2) Aligned - Lasers have aligned to the Work Order using the tool targets to within tolerance specifications (GREEN) - ( 3) Warning - Lasers have scanned tool targets, but the vision system is impaired (possibly CalibrationState=FailedCalibration) (YELLOW) - ( 4) Excluded - The projector is excluded from participating in the Work Order (BLACK)
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call
member.param: Contains the Client Id and the serial number of the projector.

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.CalibrationApi.CoreLaserServiceTargetProjection(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.TargetProjectionDto)
member.summary: Sets on/off \"Project All Targets\" or \"Show Labels\" for the specified projector. Sets the projection of remembered target locations by a specific projector on (ProjectTargets=true) or off (false); same as clicking the \"Project All Targets\" button in the projector's Projector Dashboard > Targets Tab. If ShowLabels is true, will also display the target name label as if the \"Show Labels\" checkbox was enabled under the Project All Targets button. ShowLabels is ignored if `ProjectTargets=false`. <example> TargetProjectionDto { ClientInfo (ClientInfoDto, required), ProjectorSerial (string, required), ProjectTargets (boolean, required), ShowLabels (boolean, required) } ClientInfoDto { ClientId (string, required), OriginatingClientGuid (string, optional), Type (string, optional) } </example>

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ICertificationApi.CoreLaserServiceCertifyAlignment(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.CertifyAlignmentDto)
member.summary: Performs a Certification using the specified projector and the open Work Order.
member.remarks: Same as clicking \"Certify Alignment\" in the alignment controls, Iris Client > Projector Panel > Targets Tab; Work Order must be a Certification Work Order. See \"Certification\" in Iris System Administrator Guide. Report produced can be obtained using `/WorkOrders/{workOrder}/CertificationReports` and `/WorkOrders/{workOrder}/CertificationReports/{reportId}/{file}` * **AlignBeforeCertify** - Whether to align before certifying, true or false, however true must be used to do a proper certification * **DisplayUnits** - Units used in the report. Use 'Metres', 'Centimetres', 'Millimetres', 'Yards', 'Feet', 'Inches', or 'BuildersUnits' * **ReportSoftwareVersion** - String that will be shown in the “Build” field on the report, you are responsible for supplying the version * **LocalizeTagResources** - Set as [“Certification”, “Alignment”, “Disabled”] (only legal value) * **CertificationReportTargets** - Target names of targets used in report <example> CertifyAlignmentDto { ClientInfo (ClientInfoDto, required), ProjectorSerial (string, required), AlignBeforeCertify (boolean, required), DisplayUnits (Units, optional), ReportSoftwareVersion (string, optional), LocalizeTagResources (Array[string], optional), CertificationReportTargets (Array[string], optional) } ClientInfoDto { ClientId (string, required), OriginatingClientGuid (string, optional), Type (string, optional) } </example>
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ICertificationApi.CoreLaserServiceGetCertificationReportFile(System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Serves a specific report/data file from a certification report
member.remarks: The method `/GetCertificationReportIndex` returns a list of available Certification Reports for the specified Work Order. For each report, a csv format and an HTML form is available. This method returns the actual report file specified by Report ID (the first subfolder in the URLs returned above) and the report file name, all of which are named according to: `CERT_{projector serial}_{date}_{time}`
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call
member.param: Work order identifier, corresponding to the work order folder name.
File to serve. Must be contained directly in the report folder.

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.IIrisApi.CoreLaserServiceAddManualClippingBoundaries(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ManualClippingConfigurationDto)
member.summary: Adds Work Order + Projector specific Manual Clipping Boundaries
member.remarks: See \"Manual Clipping Boundaries\" in Iris System Administrator's Guide. A Manual Clipping Boundary is defined by one or more clipping planes each specified as: * a point through which the plane passes * a normal vector, orthogonal to the plane that points \"in\" towards the projection area that is being assigned to this projector. Unlike most other API methods which operate with projectors named explicitly with serial #, clipping boundaries are best used in defined Work Cell configurations (See \"Work Cells\" and \"Projector Replacement\" in Iris Administrator's Guide), so here boundaries are specified using Projector Familiar Names instead of serial #. Manual Clipping Boundaries can be added to Work Orders that aren't even loaded; there is no `/RemoveManualClippingBoundaries` or `/EditManualClippingBoundaries` however - changes or deletion will have to be done via Iris Client: Work Order Options \"Manual Clipping Boundaries\". <example> ManualClippingConfigurationDto { ClientInfo (ClientInfoDto, optional), WorkOrderName (string, optional), ClippingBoundary (Array[ClippingBoundaryDto], optional) } ClippingBoundaryDto { Name (string, optional), ProjectorFamiliarName (string, optional), ClippingPlanes (Array[ClippingPlaneDto], optional) } ClippingPlaneDto { PlaneLocation (VertexDto, optional), PlaneNormal (VertexDto, optional) } </example> * **WorkOrderName** - name/Work Order folder * **ProjectorFamiliarName** - Familiar/friendly name of the projector - if familiar names aren't being used, use the serial number; without Familiar Names, however, the clipping boundary will have to be respecified if different projectors are used with this Work Order. * **PlaneLocation** - a plane through this point forms part of the projector's projection volume along with: * **PlaneNormal** - vector indicating \"in\" to the projector's projection volume. (See VertexDto above)
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

Manual Clipping Boundaries can be added to Work Orders that aren't even loaded; there is no `/RemoveManualClippingBoundaries` or `/EditManualClippingBoundaries` however - changes or deletion will have to be done via Iris Client: Work Order Options \"Manual Clipping Boundaries\". <example> ManualClippingConfigurationDto { ClientInfo (ClientInfoDto, optional), WorkOrderName (string, optional), ClippingBoundary (Array[ClippingBoundaryDto], optional) } ClippingBoundaryDto { Name (string, optional), ProjectorFamiliarName (string, optional), ClippingPlanes (Array[ClippingPlaneDto], optional) } ClippingPlaneDto { PlaneLocation (VertexDto, optional), PlaneNormal (VertexDto, optional) } </example> * **WorkOrderName** - name/Work Order folder * **ProjectorFamiliarName** - Familiar/friendly name of the projector - if familiar names aren't being used, use the serial number; without Familiar Names, however, the clipping boundary will have to be respecified if different projectors are used with this Work Order. * **PlaneLocation** - a plane through this point forms part of the projector's projection volume along with: * **PlaneNormal** - vector indicating \"in\" to the projector's projection volume. (See VertexDto above)

member.summary: Saves target scan and target exclusion to the Work Order.
member.remarks: Same as the \"Lock Configuration\" button in the Projector Panel > Targets Tab alignment controls. member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.IProjectionApi.CoreLaserServiceAddProjectPolygon(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ProjectPolygonDto)
member.summary: Adds raw PLY data directly to the Work Order's Display List and Process Step List.
member.remarks: Accepts projection data in raw coordinates (same as Work Order PLY files). When projecting, Iris will sweep from the first point to the last (if you want a closed polygon, repeat the first coordinate as the last) See \"Ad-Hoc Projection Entities\" in the Integrators Guide for why/when you'd want to use this vs. `/ProjectEntities` Any projections added here (with a name provided) show in the Iris Process Step List (if Iris is open), are visualized in the 3D/CAD view and are automatically projected by the appropriate lasers. Projections added via API show as dark green in the 3D/CAD view, and the selection highlight in the Process Step List is dark green as well (steps that existed in the Work Order when opened are highlighted in light green). Steps added via `/AddProjectPolygon` immediately replace any contents of the Work Order's Display List. Note that if you do not provide a Name, the new step is NOT added to the Work Order's Process Step List. Selection of steps in the Work Order's Process Step List is unaffected by this method; Next/Previous commands will still be operating on whichever steps were previously selected (in an open Iris Client, or using `/SetCurrentSelectionSteps`.) * **Name** - If provided, is the ply name as shown in Iris' Process Step List; does not have to be unique; methods that require named process steps (like `/RemoveProjectPolygons` and `/RemoveEntities`) may not behave as expected if the specified process step exists more than once; in most cases, the first occurrence of that step name will be addressed only. member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.IProjectionApi.CoreLaserServiceProjectEntities(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ProjectEntitiesDto)
member.summary: Adds new process steps, modifies existing process steps, selects and projects them.
member.remarks: Adds ad-hoc or temporary process steps to the open Work Order or modifies(1) existing process steps. Existing process steps are specified by the provided `EntityUniqueId` or by `EntityName`; if `EntityName` is not unique, the first with that name will be modified. If `EntityUniqueId` or `EntityName` do not match an existing step in the open Work Order, a new step with those parameters is created. `PlyBlocks`, if provided, will create projection/polygon actions, `TextBlocks`, if provided, will create projected text step actions. (See \"Iris Authoring\" in the Operator Guide.) If neither (valid) `PlyBlock` or `TextBlock` is provided, no steps will be created (i.e. no empty steps are generated.) or modified; if the specified `EntityUniqueId` or `EntityName` reference an existing process step, it is not switched to (selected and displayed in the Display List). To simply change Work Order selection/projection to an existing process step see `/ProjectEntityById` and `/ProjectEntityByName` **IgnoreNormals** - if true, the system will attempt to project all polygons or text in this new or modified step regardless of surface normals **AppendProjection** - if true, the step entities added via this method are added to the Work Order's active Display List and Process Step selection; if false, all existing laser projections and step selections are replaced by these new or modified entities. **PlyUnits** (required) - units for specified polygon or text coordinates; **PlyBlock** - a collection of `Points`, each with a coordinate and surface normal at that coordinate. Remember, in order to project a closed polygon the last coordinate must equal the first. The `IsCrosshair` attribute will include this polygon in the collection that can be toggled off and on with the Options > Crosshairs feature. **TextBlock** - Projected Text - both the text to display itself, and 3 points to define the origin, orientation, and projection plane of the Projected Text chevron (the angle icon used to locate and toggle Projected Text. The 3 coordinates of the chevron, in order, are bottom-left, vertex, and upper-left. The plane defined by the coordinates of the text chevron becomes the projection plane for the text. The size of the chevron is used for text size. Only a subset of ASCII characters are supported by the Projected Text laser font: `a-z A-Z 0-9 \\_ . , ? \\! ; : \\- \\+ \\* / \\\\ \\| \\( \\) { } [ ] \\# @ \\~ `. For more information on defining projected text see \"Iris Authoring\" in the Operator Guide. **ActionType** - (optional) the step actions to be tracked for these entities. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations, or use 'Polygon'. Legal actions are from the supported ply actions in the Iris Authoring Guide. **AdditionalProperties** - (optional) a dictionary capable of holding any properties that don't fit into a set category. For example, the duration of a countdown timer. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations * **Operation** - Typically use 'ProjectSkipInspectingCurrent' for updating the projection. Other options are 'UpdateDisplayOnly' for client UI updates, 'ProjectAfterInspectingCurrent' for updating multiple services when adding a camera action, 'ProjectOnly' for projector projection update only (currently only pick n project is using this flag), and 'ProjectAfterLoggingInfo'. * **ActionOverrideInfo** - (optional) the user override information for failed inspection actions. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations. * **ActionTrackInfo** - (optional) the display step actions to be tracked before project the new entities. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations. * **EntityUniqueId** - the unique ID of the step; if creating a new ad hoc step this must be distinct from any ids already in use by the system; ids can be retrieved using `/GetCurrentProjectionEntities` or `/GetProjectionData` if needed. * **EntityName** - the name of the step; if the step name specified is NOT unique, the first step that matches the name is used; must match the EntityUniqueId if modifying an existing step. See \"Ad-hoc Projections\" in the Integrators Reference. (1) *No changes to the Process Step List, projection (`.ply`) file made by this endpoint will be saved, even if the Work Order is saved in Iris Client.*
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

Specified removed entities are removed from the Display List and their visualization is removed from the 3D/CAD View. If the named process step was NOT added by `/ProjectEntities`, then it is NOT removed from the Work Order's Process Step List. Cannot remove layers; although if this method removes all entities within a layer, the layer is removed as well. **EntityNames** - Names of the steps to remove. If the step name specified is NOT unique, the first step with that name is removed; if duplicate step or layer names are a possibility, use the methods `/GetCurrentProjectionEntities` or `/GetWorkOrderEntityAccessInfo` to determine the specific `EntityUniqueID`, then use `/RemoveEntitiesWithId` *Note** this method can only remove entities added using `/AddEntity`. To remove ad-hoc projection coordinates added using `/AddProjectPolygon`, use `/RemoveProjectPolygons` or `/RemoveProjectPolygonsWithId`. Named steps that were in the Work Order when it was opened are NOT removed via this method (in essence, Work Order contents cannot be modified by API calls) * **RemoveCrosshairs** - if true, will remove ONLY the Entities with the `IsCrosshair` attribute also set to true; in effect, this can be used to trigger the same effect as toggling Crosshairs off in Iris (Options menu). * **EntityIds** - this field is **obsolete** because it was poorly named. It has always required the name of the polygon to remove, not the id. While it can be used if provided with the name for backwards compatibility, any new implementation should be using **EntityNames** instead. If you want to use **EntityNames**, then you should completely remove **EntityIds** by deleting the following code: <example> \"EntityIds\": [ \"string\" ] </example> Do **not** use both fields as EntityIDs will replace EntityNames if they are both provided.

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.IProjectionApi.CoreLaserServiceAddProjectPolygonAsync(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ProjectPolygonDto)
member.summary: Adds raw PLY data directly to the Work Order's Display List and Process Step List.
member.remarks: Accepts projection data in raw coordinates (same as Work Order PLY files). When projecting, Iris will sweep from the first point to the last (if you want a closed polygon, repeat the first coordinate as the last) See \"Ad-Hoc Projection Entities\" in the Integrators Guide for why/when you'd want to use this vs. `/ProjectEntities` Any projections added here (with a name provided) show in the Iris Process Step List (if Iris is open), are visualized in the 3D/CAD view and are automatically projected by the appropriate lasers. Projections added via API show as dark green in the 3D/CAD view, and the selection highlight in the Process Step List is dark green as well (steps that existed in the Work Order when opened are highlighted in light green). Steps added via `/AddProjectPolygon` immediately replace any contents of the Work Order's Display List. Note that if you do not provide a Name, the new step is NOT added to the Work Order's Process Step List. Selection of steps in the Work Order's Process Step List is unaffected by this method; Next/Previous commands will still be operating on whichever steps were previously selected (in an open Iris Client, or using `/SetCurrentSelectionSteps`.) * **Name** - If provided, is the ply name as shown in Iris' Process Step List; does not have to be unique; methods that require named process steps (like `/RemoveProjectPolygons` and `/RemoveEntities`) may not behave as expected if the specified process step exists more than once; in most cases, the first occurrence of that step name will be addressed only. Where duplicate step or layer names are expected, `EntityUniqueID` specific endpoints (e.g. `/RemoveEntitiesWithID`, `/RemoveProjectPolygonsWithId`) can be used, after retrieving step and layer `EntityUniqueID` values using `/GetCurrentProjectionEntities` or `/GetWorkOrderEntityAccessInfo`. * **ID** - Corresponds to EntityUniqueID; the identifier that uniquely identifies steps - MUST be unique in the Work Order. If not provided, is created and assigned automatically. This is the parameter used by `/RemoveProjectPolygonsWithId`. * **Units** - Units the projection points in 'NormalPointsData' are specified in; does not have to match that of the open Work Order, Iris will convert; see \"Units\" in Integrators Guide * **Type** - use \"Polygon\"; other values are unsupported at this time. * **NormalPointsData** - string containing raw projection coordinates (.ply file format), one line per projection point with 2,3 or 6 values space separated: 2 values = 2D point (z=0) 3 values = 3D point (x,y,z); 6 values = 3D point (x,y,z) with normal vector (a,b,c - do not have to be normalized) <example> 0.684006 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 1.242432 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 1.242432 6.380219 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 6.380219 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 4.387138 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 4.387138 8.162716 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 6.938428 8.162716 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 6.938428 11.082913 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 5.713986 11.082913 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 5.713986 11.582541 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 7.913908 11.582541 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 7.913908 15.575661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 15.575661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 13.949827 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 0.684006 13.949827 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 0.684006 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 </example> **Note** - step and layer \"uniqueness\" and the behaviour of this method depends on BOTH the step/layer NAME (argument `Name`) and its unique Identifier EntityUniqueId (argument `Id`). If you specify: EXISTING/NO Name + EXISTING Id - this is IGNORED; to \"switch\" to an existing step with either Name or Id, use `/AddEntity`. EXISTING Name + NEW Id - creates new (duplicate) step named Name; discards the provided Id and auto-generates new one EXISTING Name + NO Id - creates new (duplicate) step named Name; auto-generates the Id NEW Name + EXISTING Id - creates new (new) step named Name; IGNORES the provided Id and auto-generates new one NEW Name + NEW Id - creates new (new) step named Name; IGNORES the provided Id and auto-generates new one NEW Name + NO Id - creates a new step named Name, auto-generates Id See \"Process Step Uniqueness\" in the Integrator's Guide for more details. Also note that any Id (EntityUniqueId) automatically generated will be decreasing integrators (-1, -2, -3)...

This is the parameter used by `/RemoveProjectPolygonsWithId`. * **Units** - Units the projection points in 'NormalPointsData' are specified in; does not have to match that of the open Work Order, Iris will convert; see \"Units\" in Integrators Guide * **Type** - use \"Polygon\"; other values are unsupported at this time. * **NormalPointsData** - string containing raw projection coordinates (.ply file format), one line per projection point with 2,3 or 6 values space separated: 2 values = 2D point (z=0) 3 values = 3D point (x,y,z); 6 values = 3D point (x,y,z) with normal vector (a,b,c - do not have to be normalized) <example> 0.684006 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 1.242432 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 1.242432 6.380219 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 6.380219 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 4.387138 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 4.387138 8.162716 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 6.938428 8.162716 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 6.938428 11.082913 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 5.713986 11.082913 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 5.713986 11.582541 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 7.913908 11.582541 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 7.913908 15.575661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 15.575661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 13.949827 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 0.684006 13.949827 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 0.684006 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 </example> **Note** - step and layer \"uniqueness\" and the behaviour of this method depends on BOTH the step/layer NAME (argument `Name`) and its unique Identifier EntityUniqueId (argument `Id`). If you specify: EXISTING/NO Name + EXISTING Id - this is IGNORED; to \"switch\" to an existing step with either Name or Id, use `/AddEntity`. EXISTING Name + NEW Id - creates new (duplicate) step named Name; discards the provided Id and auto-generates new one EXISTING Name + NO Id - creates new (duplicate) step named Name; auto-generates the Id NEW Name + EXISTING Id - creates new (new) step named Name; IGNORES the provided Id and auto-generates new one NEW Name + NEW Id - creates new (new) step named Name; IGNORES the provided Id and auto-generates new one NEW Name + NO Id - creates a new step named Name, auto-generates Id See \"Process Step Uniqueness\" in the Integrator's Guide for more details. Also note that any Id (EntityUniqueId) automatically generated will be decreasing integrators (-1, -2, -3)...

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.IProjectionApi.CoreLaserServiceProjectEntitiesAsync(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ProjectEntitiesDto)
member.summary: Adds new process steps, modifies existing process steps, selects and projects them.
member.remarks: Adds ad-hoc or temporary process steps to the open Work Order or modifies(1) existing process steps. Existing process steps are specified by the provided `EntityUniqueId` or by `EntityName`; if `EntityName` is not unique, the first with that name will be modified. If `EntityUniqueId` or `EntityName` do not match an existing step in the open Work Order, a new step with those parameters is created. `PlyBlocks`, if provided, will create projection/polygon actions, `TextBlocks`, if provided, will create projected text step actions. (See \"Iris Authoring\" in the Operator Guide.) If neither (valid) `PlyBlock` or `TextBlock` is provided, no steps will be created (i.e. no empty steps are generated.) or modified; if the specified `EntityUniqueId` or `EntityName` reference an existing process step, it is not switched to (selected and displayed in the Display List). To simply change Work Order selection/projection to an existing process step see `/ProjectEntityById` and `/ProjectEntityByName` **IgnoreNormals** - if true, the system will attempt to project all polygons or text in this new or modified step regardless of surface normals **AppendProjection** - if true, the step entities added via this method are added to the Work Order's active Display List and Process Step selection; if false, all existing laser projections and step selections are replaced by these new or modified entities. **PlyUnits** (required) - units for specified polygon or text coordinates; **PlyBlock** - a collection of `Points`, each with a coordinate and surface normal at that coordinate. Remember, in order to project a closed polygon the last coordinate must equal the first. The `IsCrosshair` attribute will include this polygon in the collection that can be toggled off and on with the Options > Crosshairs feature. **TextBlock** - Projected Text - both the text to display itself, and 3 points to define the origin, orientation, and projection plane of the Projected Text chevron (the angle icon used to locate and toggle Projected Text. The 3 coordinates of the chevron, in order, are bottom-left, vertex, and upper-left. The plane defined by the coordinates of the text chevron becomes the projection plane for the text. The size of the chevron is used for text size. Only a subset of ASCII characters are supported by the Projected Text laser font: `a-z A-Z 0-9 \\_ . , ? \\! ; : \\- \\+ \\* / \\\\ \\| \\( \\) { } [ ] \\# @ \\~ `. For more information on defining projected text see \"Iris Authoring\" in the Operator Guide. **ActionType** - (optional) the step actions to be tracked for these entities. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations, or use 'Polygon'. Legal actions are from the supported ply actions in the Iris Authoring Guide. **AdditionalProperties** - (optional) a dictionary capable of holding any properties that don't fit into a set category. For example, the duration of a countdown timer. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations * **Operation** - Typically use 'ProjectSkipInspectingCurrent' for updating the projection. Other options are 'UpdateDisplayOnly' for client UI updates, 'ProjectAfterInspectingCurrent' for updating multiple services when adding a camera action, 'ProjectOnly' for projector projection update only (currently only pick n project is using this flag), and 'ProjectAfterLoggingInfo'. * **ActionOverrideInfo** - (optional) the user override information for failed inspection actions. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations. * **ActionTrackInfo** - (optional) the display step actions to be tracked before project the new entities. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations. * **EntityUniqueId** - the unique ID of the step; if creating a new ad hoc step this must be distinct from any ids already in use by the system; ids can be retrieved using `/GetCurrentProjectionEntities` or `/GetProjectionData` if needed. * **EntityName** - the name of the step; if the step name specified is NOT unique, the first step that matches the name is used; must match the EntityUniqueId if modifying an existing step. See \"Ad-hoc Projections\" in the Integrators Reference. (1) *No changes to the Process Step List, projection (`.ply`) file made by this endpoint will be saved, even if the Work Order is saved in Iris Client.*

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.IProjectionApi.CoreLaserServiceRemoveEntitiesAsync(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.RemoveEntitiesDto)
member.summary: Removes the named process step(s) from active projection in the the Work Order's Display List and the Process Step List if applicable.
member.remarks: Removes the ply or process step list entities by NAME that have been added by `/ProjectEntities`. Specified removed entities are removed from the Display List and their visualization is removed from the 3D/CAD View. If the removed step/entity is part of the current Process Step List selection, the previous step is added to the selection automatically (if applicable); no need to call `/SetCurrentSelectionSteps`. If the named process step was NOT added by `/ProjectEntities`, then it is NOT removed from the Work Order's Process Step List. Cannot remove layers; although if this method removes all entities within a layer, the layer is removed as well. **EntityNames** - Names of the steps to remove. If the step name specified is NOT unique, the first step with that name is removed; if duplicate step or layer names are a possibility, use the methods `/GetCurrentProjectionEntities` or `/GetWorkOrderEntityAccessInfo` to determine the specific `EntityUniqueID`, then use `/RemoveEntitiesWithId` *Note** this method can only remove entities added using `/AddEntity`. To remove ad-hoc projection coordinates added using `/AddProjectPolygon`, use `/RemoveProjectPolygons` or `/RemoveProjectPolygonsWithId`. Named steps that were in the Work Order when it was opened are NOT removed via this method (in essence, Work Order contents cannot be modified by API calls) * **RemoveCrosshairs** - if true, will remove ONLY the Entities with the `IsCrosshair` attribute also set to true; in effect, this can be used to trigger the same effect as toggling Crosshairs off in Iris (Options menu). * **EntityIds** - this field is **obsolete** because it was poorly named. It has always required the name of the polygon to remove, not the id. While it can be used if provided with the name for backwards compatibility, any new implementation should be using **EntityNames** instead. If you want to use **EntityNames**, then you should completely remove **EntityIds** by deleting the following code: <example> \"EntityIds\": [ \"string\" ] </example> Do **not** use both fields as EntityIDs will replace EntityNames if they are both provided.

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ProjectionApi.CoreLaserServiceAddProjectPolygon(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ProjectPolygonDto)
member.summary: Adds raw PLY data directly to the Work Order's Display List and Process Step List. Accepts projection data in raw coordinates (same as Work Order PLY files). When projecting, Iris will sweep from the first point to the last (if you want a closed polygon, repeat the first coordinate as the last) See \"Ad-Hoc Projection Entities\" in the Integrators Guide for why/when you'd want to use this vs. `/ProjectEntities` Any projections added here (with a name provided) show in the Iris Process Step List (if Iris is open), are visualized in the 3D/CAD view and are automatically projected by the appropriate lasers. Projections added via API show as dark green in the 3D/CAD view, and the selection highlight in the Process Step List is dark green as well (steps that existed in the Work Order when opened are highlighted in light green). Steps added via `/AddProjectPolygon` immediately replace any contents of the Work Order's Display List. Note that if you do not provide a Name, the new step is NOT added to the Work Order's Process Step List. Selection of steps in the Work Order's Process Step List is unaffected by this method; Next/Previous commands will still be operating on whichever steps were previously selected (in an open Iris Client, or using `/SetCurrentSelectionSteps`.) * **Name** - If provided, is the ply name as shown in Iris' Process Step List; does not have to be unique; methods that require named process steps (like `/RemoveProjectPolygons` and `/RemoveEntities`) may not behave as expected if the specified process step exists more than once; in most cases, the first occurrence of that step name will be addressed only. Where duplicate step or layer names are expected, `EntityUniqueID` specific endpoints (e.g. `/RemoveEntitiesWithID`, `/RemoveProjectPolygonsWithId`) can be used, after retrieving step and layer `EntityUniqueID` values using `/GetCurrentProjectionEntities` or `/GetWorkOrderEntityAccessInfo`. * **ID** - Corresponds to EntityUniqueID; the identifier that uniquely identifies steps - MUST be unique in the Work Order. If not provided, is created and assigned automatically. This is the parameter used by `/RemoveProjectPolygonsWithId`. * **Units** - Units the projection points in 'NormalPointsData' are specified in; does not have to match that of the open Work Order, Iris will convert; see \"Units\" in Integrators Guide * **Type** - use \"Polygon\"; other values are unsupported at this time. * **NormalPointsData** - string containing raw projection coordinates (.ply file format), one line per projection point with 2,3 or 6 values space separated: 2 values = 2D point (z=0) 3 values = 3D point (x,y,z); 6 values = 3D point (x,y,z) with normal vector (a,b,c - do not have to be normalized) <example> 0.684006 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 1.242432 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 1.242432 6.380219 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 6.380219 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 4.387138 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 4.387138 8.162716 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 6.938428 8.162716 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 6.938428 11.082913 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 5.713986 11.082913 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 5.713986 11.582541 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 7.913908 11.582541 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 7.913908 15.575661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 15.575661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 3.505415 13.949827 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 0.684006 13.949827 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 0.684006 9.976661 0.100000 0.000000 0.000000 1 </example> **Note** - step and layer \"uniqueness\" and the behaviour of this method depends on BOTH the step/layer NAME (argument `Name`) and its unique Identifier EntityUniqueId (argument `Id`). If you specify: EXISTING/NO Name + EXISTING Id - this is IGNORED; to \"switch\" to an existing step with either Name or Id, use `/AddEntity`. EXISTING Name + NEW Id - creates new (duplicate) step named Name; discards the provided Id and auto-generates new one EXISTING Name + NO Id - creates new (duplicate) step named Name; auto-generates the Id NEW Name + EXISTING Id - creates new (new) step named Name; IGNORES the provided Id and auto-generates new one NEW Name + NEW Id - creates new (new) step named Name; IGNORES the provided Id and auto-generates new one NEW Name + NO Id - creates a new step named Name, auto-generates Id See \"Process Step Uniqueness\" in the Integrator's Guide for more details. Also note that any Id (EntityUniqueId) automatically generated will be decreasing integrators (-1, -2, -3)...
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

If you specify: EXISTING/NO Name + EXISTING Id - this is IGNORED; to \"switch\" to an existing step with either Name or Id, use `/AddEntity`. EXISTING Name + NEW Id - creates new (duplicate) step named Name; discards the provided Id and auto-generates new one EXISTING Name + NO Id - creates new (duplicate) step named Name; auto-generates the Id NEW Name + EXISTING Id - creates new (new) step named Name; IGNORES the provided Id and auto-generates new one NEW Name + NEW Id - creates new (new) step named Name; IGNORES the provided Id and auto-generates new one NEW Name + NO Id - creates a new step named Name, auto-generates Id See \"Process Step Uniqueness\" in the Integrator's Guide for more details. member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ProjectionApi.CoreLaserServiceProjectEntities(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ProjectEntitiesDto)
member.summary: Adds new process steps, modifies existing process steps, selects and projects them. Adds ad-hoc or temporary process steps to the open Work Order or modifies(1) existing process steps. Existing process steps are specified by the provided `EntityUniqueId` or by `EntityName`; if `EntityName` is not unique, the first with that name will be modified. If `EntityUniqueId` or `EntityName` do not match an existing step in the open Work Order, a new step with those parameters is created. `PlyBlocks`, if provided, will create projection/polygon actions, `TextBlocks`, if provided, will create projected text step actions. (See \"Iris Authoring\" in the Operator Guide.) If neither (valid) `PlyBlock` or `TextBlock` is provided, no steps will be created (i.e. no empty steps are generated.) or modified; if the specified `EntityUniqueId` or `EntityName` reference an existing process step, it is not switched to (selected and displayed in the Display List). To simply change Work Order selection/projection to an existing process step see `/ProjectEntityById` and `/ProjectEntityByName` **IgnoreNormals** - if true, the system will attempt to project all polygons or text in this new or modified step regardless of surface normals **AppendProjection** - if true, the step entities added via this method are added to the Work Order's active Display List and Process Step selection; if false, all existing laser projections and step selections are replaced by these new or modified entities. **PlyUnits** (required) - units for specified polygon or text coordinates; **PlyBlock** - a collection of `Points`, each with a coordinate and surface normal at that coordinate. Remember, in order to project a closed polygon the last coordinate must equal the first. The `IsCrosshair` attribute will include this polygon in the collection that can be toggled off and on with the Options > Crosshairs feature. **TextBlock** - Projected Text - both the text to display itself, and 3 points to define the origin, orientation, and projection plane of the Projected Text chevron (the angle icon used to locate and toggle Projected Text. The 3 coordinates of the chevron, in order, are bottom-left, vertex, and upper-left. The plane defined by the coordinates of the text chevron becomes the projection plane for the text. The size of the chevron is used for text size. Only a subset of ASCII characters are supported by the Projected Text laser font: `a-z A-Z 0-9 \\_ . , ? \\! ; : \\- \\+ \\* / \\\\ \\| \\( \\) { } [ ] \\# @ \\~ `. For more information on defining projected text see \"Iris Authoring\" in the Operator Guide. **ActionType** - (optional) the step actions to be tracked for these entities. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations, or use 'Polygon'. Legal actions are from the supported ply actions in the Iris Authoring Guide. **AdditionalProperties** - (optional) a dictionary capable of holding any properties that don't fit into a set category. For example, the duration of a countdown timer. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations * **Operation** - Typically use 'ProjectSkipInspectingCurrent' for updating the projection. Other options are 'UpdateDisplayOnly' for client UI updates, 'ProjectAfterInspectingCurrent' for updating multiple services when adding a camera action, 'ProjectOnly' for projector projection update only (currently only pick n project is using this flag), and 'ProjectAfterLoggingInfo'. * **ActionOverrideInfo** - (optional) the user override information for failed inspection actions. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations. * **ActionTrackInfo** - (optional) the display step actions to be tracked before project the new entities. This section can be removed for 'ProjectOnly' operations. * **EntityUniqueId** - the unique ID of the step; if creating a new ad hoc step this must be distinct from any ids already in use by the system; ids can be retrieved using `/GetCurrentProjectionEntities` or `/GetProjectionData` if needed. * **EntityName** - the name of the step; if the step name specified is NOT unique, the first step that matches the name is used; must match the EntityUniqueId if modifying an existing step. member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ProjectionApi.CoreLaserServiceRemoveEntities(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.RemoveEntitiesDto)
member.summary: Removes the named process step(s) from active projection in the the Work Order's Display List and the Process Step List if applicable. Removes the ply or process step list entities by NAME that have been added by `/ProjectEntities`. Specified removed entities are removed from the Display List and their visualization is removed from the 3D/CAD View. If the removed step/entity is part of the current Process Step List selection, the previous step is added to the selection automatically (if applicable); no need to call `/SetCurrentSelectionSteps`. If the named process step was NOT added by `/ProjectEntities`, then it is NOT removed from the Work Order's Process Step List. Cannot remove layers; although if this method removes all entities within a layer, the layer is removed as well. **EntityNames** - Names of the steps to remove. If the step name specified is NOT unique, the first step with that name is removed; if duplicate step or layer names are a possibility, use the methods `/GetCurrentProjectionEntities` or `/GetWorkOrderEntityAccessInfo` to determine the specific `EntityUniqueID`, then use `/RemoveEntitiesWithId` *Note** this method can only remove entities added using `/AddEntity`. To remove ad-hoc projection coordinates added using `/AddProjectPolygon`, use `/RemoveProjectPolygons` or `/RemoveProjectPolygonsWithId`. Named steps that were in the Work Order when it was opened are NOT removed via this method (in essence, Work Order contents cannot be modified by API calls) * **RemoveCrosshairs** - if true, will remove ONLY the Entities with the `IsCrosshair` attribute also set to true; in effect, this can be used to trigger the same effect as toggling Crosshairs off in Iris (Options menu). * **EntityIds** - this field is **obsolete** because it was poorly named. It has always required the name of the polygon to remove, not the id. While it can be used if provided with the name for backwards compatibility, any new implementation should be using **EntityNames** instead. If you want to use **EntityNames**, then you should completely remove **EntityIds** by deleting the following code: <example> \"EntityIds\": [ \"string\" ] </example> Do **not** use both fields as EntityIDs will replace EntityNames if they are both provided.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.summary: Removes the named process step(s) from active projection in the the Work Order's Display List and the Process Step List if applicable. Specified removed entities are removed from the Display List and their visualization is removed from the 3D/CAD View. If the removed step/entity is part of the current Process Step List selection, the previous step is added to the selection automatically (if applicable); no need to call `/SetCurrentSelectionSteps`. If the named process step was NOT added by `/ProjectEntities`, then it is NOT removed from the Work Order's Process Step List. Cannot remove layers; although if this method removes all entities within a layer, the layer is removed as well. **EntityNames** - Names of the steps to remove. If the step name specified is NOT unique, the first step with that name is removed; if duplicate step or layer names are a possibility, use the methods `/GetCurrentProjectionEntities` or `/GetWorkOrderEntityAccessInfo` to determine the specific `EntityUniqueID`, then use `/RemoveEntitiesWithId` *Note** this method can only remove entities added using `/AddEntity`. To remove ad-hoc projection coordinates added using `/AddProjectPolygon`, use `/RemoveProjectPolygons` or `/RemoveProjectPolygonsWithId`. Named steps that were in the Work Order when it was opened are NOT removed via this method (in essence, Work Order contents cannot be modified by API calls) * **RemoveCrosshairs** - if true, will remove ONLY the Entities with the `IsCrosshair` attribute also set to true; in effect, this can be used to trigger the same effect as toggling Crosshairs off in Iris (Options menu). * **EntityIds** - this field is **obsolete** because it was poorly named. It has always required the name of the polygon to remove, not the id. While it can be used if provided with the name for backwards compatibility, any new implementation should be using **EntityNames** instead. If you want to use **EntityNames**, then you should completely remove **EntityIds** by deleting the following code: <example> \"EntityIds\": [ \"string\" ] </example> Do **not** use both fields as EntityIDs will replace EntityNames if they are both provided.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ProjectionApi.CoreLaserServiceRemoveProjectPolygons(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.RemoveEntitiesDto)
member.summary: Removes raw PLY data by NAME from the Work Order. Removes the specified entities by NAME that have been added by `/AddProjectPolygon`. Specified removed polygons are removed from the Display List and their visualization is removed from the 3D/CAD View. If the removed step/entity is part of the current Process Step List selection, the previous step is added to the selection automatically (if applicable); no need to call `/SetCurrentSelectionSteps`. IF the specified step name is not unique, then the first step with that name is removed. See also `/RemoveProjectPolygonsWithId` **Note** this method can only remove entities added using `/AddProjectPolygon`. To remove ad-hoc projection entities added using `/ProjectEntities`, use `/RemoveEntities`. * **RemoveCrosshairs** - if true, will remove ONLY the Polygons with the `IsCrosshair` attribute also set to true; in effect, this can be used to trigger the same effect as toggling Crosshairs off in Iris (Options menu). * **EntityIds** - this field is **obsolete** because it was poorly named. It has always required the name of the polygon to remove, not the id. While it can be used if provided with the name for backwards compatibility, any new implementation should be using **EntityNames** instead. If you want to use **EntityNames**, then you should completely remove **EntityIds** by deleting the following code: <example> \"EntityIds\": [ \"string\" ] </example> Do **not** use both fields as EntityIDs will replace EntityNames if they are both provided.

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ISystemApi.CoreLaserServiceConnectClient(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientInfoDto)
member.summary: Registers this client with the Virtek Server.
member.remarks: Registers this client, uniquely identified by \"OriginatingClientGuid\" as part of the client session named by \"ClientId\". If an active client has already initialized the session under that ClientId, this client is registered to use the same resources (Work Order, projectors, Work Cell, etc.) Attempting to connect a second active client to the session ClientId will return an error. Active clients must send keep-alive messages every 2 minutes - see `/SendHeartBeat`. Passive clients do not have to send keep-alive messages. There is no restriction on the number of passive clients that can connect to a session. /DisconnectClient must be called for each client to release resources. i.e. Each passive client as well as the active client Each client can provide an additional identifier, OriginatingClientGUID which should be unique to each client (and it doesn't have to be an actual GUID it can be any unique string); the API will not complain if this parameter is not unique, however in the system / Work Order logs that record activity, you will not be able to differentiate between API client actions unless they are. In order for Reflection to work, OriginatingClientGUID must be unique (OriginatingClientGUID is used to determine which clients to send update events to.) All clients that share ClientID MUST be open prior to opening the Work Order or doing anything else to the Work Order, otherwise, echo/reflection synchronization can't be guaranteed. <example> ClientInfoDto { ClientId (string, required), OriginatingClientGuid (string, optional), Type (string, optional) } // example: ClientInfoDto { \"Client1\", \"2D668C86-07A3-4C5A-8BEF-DF161A0F50A0\", \"Passive\" } </example>
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ISystemApi.CoreLaserServiceDisconnectClient(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientInfoDto)
member.summary: De-registers this client with the Virtek Server and clears resources allocated if applicable.
member.remarks: If this client is passive, and the session's active client remains open (and responding with heartbeats), then the session resources will remain allocated. Once the last client closes for a specified ClientID, the system will close any associated Work Order, files, and frees any other system resources (projector reservations, etc.) as required. If an active client terminates abnormally, eventually the lack of keep-alive messages will cause the server to pause projection and eventually attempt cleanup; If a passive client never calls /DisconnectClient, the server may never perform cleanup - this may manifest in projectors that are strangely unavailable or are unresponsive, or work orders that are unavailable for opening or editing. - in this case, restarting the services will be required in Virtek Server Manager. For proper clean up of resources, /DisconnectClient must be called for each client that has connected to the server. To find which clients are connected to the server, use /GetCurrentClients.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ISystemApi.CoreLaserServiceGetProjectionConfiguration
member.summary: Retrieves a selection of projection quality/accuracy parameters in use by the system.
member.remarks: * **PartIntersectionToleranceMM**: When creating geometry from input points(from files), two points are considered the same if they are less than this distance apart (\"heals\" two different polygons together); how close a point is to a line before it is considered to intersect the line. * **EnableCrosshairProjections:**: When enabled (true) projection clients will overlay surface planar crosshairs over top of circular features (including holes). Configured by default in Virtek Server Manager > Iris Client > Projection Options \"Project Crosshairs\"; note this does not reflect whether or not crosshairs are actively being projected, as the Operator can enable/disable this in Iris Client > Options > \"Project circle crosshairs\" * **DisplayCrosshairProjections:** When enabled (true) shows the location of crosshair projections in the Iris CAD model view; regardless of whether their (laser) projection is enabled by default (see EnableCrosshairProjections above) or is currently activated by Iris Client > Options > project circle crosshairs. * BreakIntersectingPolygons - Internal use only * **CrosshairRadiusFitToleranceMillimeters** - how far from \"circular\" a circle point can be before it is no longer considered a circle (for crosshair purposes) * **CrosshairCoplanarDeviationAngleTolerance** - how flat points on a circle have to be before it is no longer considered a circle (for crosshair purposes) * **CrosshairMinimumNumberOfPointsInCircle** - a circle (for crosshair purposes) has to have at least this many points * **ImageErrorTolerance** - the fundamental accuracy parameter; the laser is guaranteed to never sweep further away than this from nominal; lower values will result in slower laser sweeps and higher flicker * **TextErrorTolerance** - same as above but for Projected Text; lower values = sharper text characters but with more flicker * **FocusToleranceFactor** - how accurate Focus Of Attention projections are vs. normal, specified as an ImageErrorTolerance multiplier - e.g. 10x more accurate, specify 0.1 for this parameter * **ObjectFocus** - when true, Focus of Attention reduces focus to polygons, entities overlapping the retro; when false, Focus of Attention is a circular radius around the retro hit * **FocusCheckPeriodMilliseconds** - Focus of Attention - how frequently FoA checks for persistence of the retro material * **FocusTrackPeriodMilliseconds** - Laser octagon cursor - how frequently the laser octagon tracking checks for retro presence * IsFoaDetailedDebugging - Internal use only * **ShiftTranslationMillimetres** - distance projection will be shifted in mm. * **ShiftRotationDegrees** - number of degrees projection will be rotated Some of these parameters can be modified via API while the system is running. See `/UpdateServerConfiguration`.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ISystemApi.CoreLaserServiceSendHeartBeat(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientIdDto)
member.summary: Sends a heartbeat to Virtek Server; active clients which don't, will have projection paused, then be disconnected.
member.remarks: This is only required of active clients (see \"Active/Passive Clients and ClientID\" in Integration Guide) * On first connection of an active client, Virtek Server monitors for periodic heartbeats from the client in liu of any actual commands. * If none are received after 2 minutes, Virtek Server pauses projection for that client but will resume projection if it receives any subsequent heartbeat. * If no heartbeat is received after 30 minutes all session resources for the active client are released as though the Client had disconnected/closed.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ISystemApi.CoreLaserServiceDisconnectClientAsync(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientInfoDto)
member.summary: De-registers this client with the Virtek Server and clears resources allocated if applicable.
member.remarks: If this client is passive, and the session's active client remains open (and responding with heartbeats), then the session resources will remain allocated. Once the last client closes for a specified ClientID, the system will close any associated Work Order, files, and frees any other system resources (projector reservations, etc.) as required. If an active client terminates abnormally, eventually the lack of keep-alive messages will cause the server to pause projection and eventually attempt cleanup; If a passive client never calls /DisconnectClient, the server may never perform cleanup - this may manifest in projectors that are strangely unavailable or are unresponsive, or work orders that are unavailable for opening or editing. - in this case, restarting the services will be required in Virtek Server Manager. For proper clean up of resources, /DisconnectClient must be called for each client that has connected to the server. To find which clients are connected to the server, use /GetCurrentClients.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ISystemApi.CoreLaserServiceGetProjectionConfigurationAsync
member.summary: Retrieves a selection of projection quality/accuracy parameters in use by the system.
member.remarks: * **PartIntersectionToleranceMM**: When creating geometry from input points(from files), two points are considered the same if they are less than this distance apart (\"heals\" two different polygons together); how close a point is to a line before it is considered to intersect the line. * **EnableCrosshairProjections:**: When enabled (true) projection clients will overlay surface planar crosshairs over top of circular features (including holes). Configured by default in Virtek Server Manager > Iris Client > Projection Options \"Project Crosshairs\"; note this does not reflect whether or not crosshairs are actively being projected, as the Operator can enable/disable this in Iris Client > Options > \"Project circle crosshairs\" * **DisplayCrosshairProjections:** When enabled (true) shows the location of crosshair projections in the Iris CAD model view; regardless of whether their (laser) projection is enabled by default (see EnableCrosshairProjections above) or is currently activated by Iris Client > Options > project circle crosshairs. * BreakIntersectingPolygons - Internal use only * **CrosshairRadiusFitToleranceMillimeters** - how far from \"circular\" a circle point can be before it is no longer considered a circle (for crosshair purposes) * **CrosshairCoplanarDeviationAngleTolerance** - how flat points on a circle have to be before it is no longer considered a circle (for crosshair purposes) * **CrosshairMinimumNumberOfPointsInCircle** - a circle (for crosshair purposes) has to have at least this many points * **ImageErrorTolerance** - the fundamental accuracy parameter; the laser is guaranteed to never sweep further away than this from nominal; lower values will result in slower laser sweeps and higher flicker * **TextErrorTolerance** - same as above but for Projected Text; lower values = sharper text characters but with more flicker * **FocusToleranceFactor** - how accurate Focus Of Attention projections are vs. normal, specified as an ImageErrorTolerance multiplier - e.g. 10x more accurate, specify 0.1 for this parameter * **ObjectFocus** - when true, Focus of Attention reduces focus to polygons, entities overlapping the retro; when false, Focus of Attention is a circular radius around the retro hit * **FocusCheckPeriodMilliseconds** - Focus of Attention - how frequently FoA checks for persistence of the retro material * **FocusTrackPeriodMilliseconds** - Laser octagon cursor - how frequently the laser octagon tracking checks for retro presence * IsFoaDetailedDebugging - Internal use only * **ShiftTranslationMillimetres** - distance projection will be shifted in mm. * **ShiftRotationDegrees** - number of degrees projection will be rotated Some of these parameters can be modified via API while the system is running. See `/UpdateServerConfiguration`.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.ISystemApi.CoreLaserServiceSendHeartBeatAsync(VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Model.ClientIdDto)
member.summary: Sends a heartbeat to Virtek Server; active clients which don't, will have projection paused, then be disconnected.
member.remarks: This is only required of active clients (see \"Active/Passive Clients and ClientID\" in Integration Guide) * On first connection of an active client, Virtek Server monitors for periodic heartbeats from the client in liu of any actual commands. * If none are received after 2 minutes, Virtek Server pauses projection for that client but will resume projection if it receives any subsequent heartbeat. * If no heartbeat is received after 30 minutes all session resources for the active client are released as though the Client had disconnected/closed.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

If an active client has already initialized the session under that ClientId, this client is registered to use the same resources (Work Order, projectors, Work Cell, etc.) Attempting to connect a second active client to the session ClientId will return an error. Active clients must send keep-alive messages every 2 minutes - see `/SendHeartBeat`. Passive clients do not have to send keep-alive messages. There is no restriction on the number of passive clients that can connect to a session. /DisconnectClient must be called for each client to release resources. i.e. Each passive client as well as the active client Each client can provide an additional identifier, OriginatingClientGUID which should be unique to each client (and it doesn't have to be an actual GUID it can be any unique string); the API will not complain if this parameter is not unique, however in the system / Work Order logs that record activity, you will not be able to differentiate between API client actions unless they are. In order for Reflection to work, OriginatingClientGUID must be unique (OriginatingClientGUID is used to determine which clients to send update events to.) All clients that share ClientID MUST be open prior to opening the Work Order or doing anything else to the Work Order, otherwise, echo/reflection synchronization can't be guaranteed. <example> ClientInfoDto { ClientId (string, required), OriginatingClientGuid (string, optional), Type (string, optional) } // example: ClientInfoDto { \"Client1\", \"2D668C86-07A3-4C5A-8BEF-DF161A0F50A0\", \"Passive\" } </example>

member.summary: De-registers this client with the Virtek Server and clears resources allocated if applicable. If this client is passive, and the session's active client remains open (and responding with heartbeats), then the session resources will remain allocated. Once the last client closes for a specified ClientID, the system will close any associated Work Order, files, and frees any other system resources (projector reservations, etc.) as required. If an active client terminates abnormally, eventually the lack of keep-alive messages will cause the server to pause projection and eventually attempt cleanup; If a passive client never calls /DisconnectClient, the server may never perform cleanup - this may manifest in projectors that are strangely unavailable or are unresponsive, or work orders that are unavailable for opening or editing. - in this case, restarting the services will be required in Virtek Server Manager. For proper clean up of resources, /DisconnectClient must be called for each client that has connected to the server. To find which clients are connected to the server, use /GetCurrentClients.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call

member.name: M:VisionAndProjectionService.Swagger.Api.SystemApi.CoreLaserServiceGetProjectionConfiguration
member.summary: Retrieves a selection of projection quality/accuracy parameters in use by the system. * **PartIntersectionToleranceMM**: When creating geometry from input points(from files), two points are considered the same if they are less than this distance apart (\"heals\" two different polygons together); how close a point is to a line before it is considered to intersect the line. * **EnableCrosshairProjections:**: When enabled (true) projection clients will overlay surface planar crosshairs over top of circular features (including holes). Configured by default in Virtek Server Manager > Iris Client > Projection Options \"Project Crosshairs\"; note this does not reflect whether or not crosshairs are actively being projected, as the Operator can enable/disable this in Iris Client > Options > \"Project circle crosshairs\" * **DisplayCrosshairProjections:** When enabled (true) shows the location of crosshair projections in the Iris CAD model view; regardless of whether their (laser) projection is enabled by default (see EnableCrosshairProjections above) or is currently activated by Iris Client > Options > project circle crosshairs. * BreakIntersectingPolygons - Internal use only * **CrosshairRadiusFitToleranceMillimeters** - how far from \"circular\" a circle point can be before it is no longer considered a circle (for crosshair purposes) * **CrosshairCoplanarDeviationAngleTolerance** - how flat points on a circle have to be before it is no longer considered a circle (for crosshair purposes) * **CrosshairMinimumNumberOfPointsInCircle** - a circle (for crosshair purposes) has to have at least this many points * **ImageErrorTolerance** - the fundamental accuracy parameter; the laser is guaranteed to never sweep further away than this from nominal; lower values will result in slower laser sweeps and higher flicker * **TextErrorTolerance** - same as above but for Projected Text; lower values = sharper text characters but with more flicker * **FocusToleranceFactor** - how accurate Focus Of Attention projections are vs. normal, specified as an ImageErrorTolerance multiplier - e.g. 10x more accurate, specify 0.1 for this parameter * **ObjectFocus** - when true, Focus of Attention reduces focus to polygons, entities overlapping the retro; when false, Focus of Attention is a circular radius around the retro hit * **FocusCheckPeriodMilliseconds** - Focus of Attention - how frequently FoA checks for persistence of the retro material * **FocusTrackPeriodMilliseconds** - Laser octagon cursor - how frequently the laser octagon tracking checks for retro presence * IsFoaDetailedDebugging - Internal use only * **ShiftTranslationMillimetres** - distance projection will be shifted in mm. * **ShiftRotationDegrees** - number of degrees projection will be rotated Some of these parameters can be modified via API while the system is running. See `/UpdateServerConfiguration`.
member.exception: Thrown when fails to make API call
